decisions.what: Mark all requirements as NOT TESTABLE HERE and NOT MET
decisions.why: The lane specifies that Rat is a macOS app and its Swift code cannot be built on Linux. The analysis is performed statically. R6 is a FAIL/NOT MET, the others are analytically PASS but practically NOT TESTABLE HERE.

In RulesModel.swift, if the store.loadSet() fails, it assigns a default ruleset which triggers the didSet block of @Published var ruleSet. This immediately overwrites the rules.json file, wiping the user's rules. A patch is proposed in the report.

decisions.what: Check cross-module mapping for FAIL R6
decisions.why: The supervisor requested that for every FAIL, we check if the same behaviour exists in RatFilter/Sources and rank FAILs by user impact.

In v1.2.0, Rat no longer blocks remote addresses. Instead, it blocks local ports of live denied sockets (and all sockets of denied apps). This was verified and the documentation for R1 was updated to reflect the new behavior.
Checked if the malformed state file issue was fixed upstream in v1.2.0. It is still not fixed; RulesModel.init still triggers an overwrite on a malformed rules.json load.

decisions.what: Created parity checklist for the port
decisions.why: The supervisor requested a parity checklist mapping macOS user-visible behaviors to the Rust crates of the port, with testing ideas and platform specifics.

decisions.what: Reviewed parity checklist after v1.2.0 update
decisions.why: The parity checklist has already been generated based on v1.2.0 files.
Included explicit mapping to specific crates as requested: rat-core, rat-geo, rat-monitor-linux, rat-monitor-windows, rat-enforcer, rat-ledger, rat-daemon, rat-names, port/app.
Followed instructions to write the file accurately mapping macOS UI behavior to Rust crates of the port.
